items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bobby Starke asked me if I would like to go downtown with him... Bobby could put away a lot of juice and so could I

ctx.x: After Chick had finished the night, Bobby Starke asked me if I would like to go downtown with him to see an uncle who lived in a district called 'Hell's Kitchen'. So we took the El at 125th Street and 8th Avenue and got off somewhere downtown in the 50s on the west side. Bobby's uncle made his own moonshine and he rolled out a 5 gallon jug and invited us to help ourselves. He was very proud of Bobby and especially because he was a good musician. Bobby could put away a lot of juice and so could I, but we didn't…

When we decided to come back uptown Bobby suggested that we take a taxi and I agreed. When we arrived at 131st Street and Lenox Avenue, Bobby told the taxi driver to turn left and go in the direction of 7th Avenue. He told me to get out when the taxi stopped and to wait for him in a hallway down the street in back of the taxi and he would take care of the fare.

I thought there was something fishy about this but did as he told me. As I was going into a hallway I saw Bobby say something to the driver and walk away. I was watching what was happening but the driver could not see me. Bobby had disappeared and after a few minutes, I saw the driver get out of his taxi, look up and down the street and then get back in and drive away.
